questions.question: Which colors help riders be seen best?

options.text: Orange and red.
Green and blue.
Purple and gold.
Black and white.

questions.correctAnswerText: Orange and red.
questions.explanation: Wear bright orange, red, yellow, or green clothing to be visible to others.

questions.question: A person drinks 7 drinks in 3 hours. The body removes about 1 drink per hour. How many drinks remain in their system 3 hours after their last drink?

options.text: Two
Three
Four
Five

questions.correctAnswerText: Four
questions.explanation: Subtract the number of hours since the last drink from the total drinks consumed. A person who drank 7 drinks in 3 hours would have 4 drinks left 3 hours later.

questions.question: After mounting your motorcycle, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Make sure the mirrors are clean.
Make sure the horn works.
Close the fuel supply valve.
Make sure the clutch works smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close the fuel supply valve.
questions.explanation: After mounting, check that the clutch, throttle, horn, and brakes work. Clean the mirrors. Keep the fuel supply valve open.

questions.question: Your lane position should do everything EXCEPT:

options.text: Help you avoid road hazards.
Help you avoid other drivers' blind spots.
Help you avoid being seen by other drivers.
Increase your ability to be seen by others.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you avoid being seen by other drivers.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see and be seen. It keeps you out of other drivers' blind spots, helps you avoid hazards, protects your lane, shows your intentions, avoids wind blasts, and gives you an escape route.

questions.question: An advantage of keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles is:

options.text: You can pass danger more quickly.
You will have a narrower view so you can stay focused.
You will have more time to react to other vehicles.
You can more easily follow the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will have more time to react to other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles gives you a clearer view of hazards, more time to react, and more room to maneuver.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Avoid other road users' blind spots.
Provide a good view of the shoulder.
Provide a poor view of road hazards.
Invite others to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid other road users' blind spots.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and be seen by them. Don't stay in another driver's blind spot for long.

questions.question: Why should group riders avoid riding in pairs?

options.text: A merging driver may not see both riders.
Helmet reflections may make it hard for riders to see.
Riding in pairs does not give riders enough space to maneuver.
It is too difficult for left-side riders to exit a highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding in pairs does not give riders enough space to maneuver.
questions.explanation: In a group, motorcyclists should never ride in pairs. Neither rider will have enough room to maneuver to avoid hazards.

questions.question: The best way to stop quickly is to:

options.text: Use the front brake only.
Use the front brake first.
Release the throttle and use the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, use the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.question: Where is the front brake lever located?

options.text: On the left handgrip
On the right handgrip
By the left foot peg
By the right foot peg

questions.correctAnswerText: On the right handgrip
questions.explanation: The front brake lever is on the right handgrip. Know where all your motorcycle's controls are before you ride.

questions.question: The front brake provides what percentage of a motorcycle's total braking power?

options.text: 10 percent
25 percent
50 percent
75 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: 75 percent
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: Where is the throttle usually located?

options.text: Near the left footrest
Near the right footrest
On the left handle grip
On the right handle grip

questions.correctAnswerText: On the right handle grip
questions.explanation: The throttle is on the right handle grip. Learn where all your motorcycle's controls are before you ride.

questions.question: How often should a motorcycle operator check their mirrors?

options.text: Never
Occasionally
Frequently
More often than the amount time spent looking ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Frequently
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often. This helps you see hazards behind you.

questions.question: If you are not traveling slowly enough when shifting into a lower gear, the:

options.text: Motorcycle could lurch and the rear tire could skid.
Motorcycle could accelerate too quickly.
Front tire will likely skid.
Engine will make a loud noise.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycle could lurch and the rear tire could skid.
questions.explanation: If you shift to a lower gear while going too fast, the motorcycle will lurch forward and the rear wheel may skid.

questions.question: Riding directly alongside another vehicle is discouraged because:

options.text: You may have a difficult time getting to a highway exit.
You may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
You may block the driver's view.
It prevents other drivers from passing both of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous. You could be in the other driver's blind spot. They may move into your lane without seeing you. Also, the vehicle blocks your escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: To lessen your chances of being involved in a crash, you should:

options.text: Not use your turn signals when changing lanes.
Follow other vehicles closely.
Watch about five feet ahead of your motorcycle while riding.
Always be ready to use crash-avoidance techniques.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to use crash-avoidance techniques.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, stay visible to others. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to show your intentions. Keep space around your motorcycle. Look ahead, behind, and to the side for hazards. Always be ready to avoid danger.

questions.question: The gearshift lever is operated by:

options.text: Your right hand.
Your right foot.
Your left hand.
Your left foot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your left foot.
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Is not necessary if you have a windshield.
Only protects your eyes.
Helps protect your whole face.
Does not protect your face as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps protect your whole face.
questions.explanation: A plastic face shield protects your whole face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not a replacement for a face shield or goggles.

questions.question: Engine braking:

options.text: Is illegal.
Is slowing down by turning the engine off.
Is slowing down by downshifting.
Is not encouraged because of the damage it does to the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is slowing down by downshifting.
questions.explanation: Engine braking means shifting to a lower gear to slow down. This works like applying the brakes.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection, you should:

options.text: Assume other drivers see you, especially if they make eye contact.
Never assume other drivers see you.
Stay focused on moving through the intersection.
Speed up to make others notice you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never assume other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: Never assume that other drivers see you, even if they look at you. Drivers often look directly at motorcycles and still miss them. Always slow down when approaching an intersection.

questions.question: If you must ride over an obstacle, you should:

options.text: Decrease your speed as much as possible.
Lean the motorcycle to one side.
Speed up, if possible.
Stay on your seat and remove your feet from the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Decrease your speed as much as possible.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid an obstacle, slow down as much as you can. Approach it at a 90-degree angle if possible. Keep the motorcycle upright. Just before hitting it, ease off the throttle to lighten the front wheel.

questions.question: In general, riders should:

options.text: Pick one lane position and always use it.
Change lane positions frequently to prevent boredom.
Choose a lane position that gives them the most space around their bike.
Never use the center lane position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Choose a lane position that gives them the most space around their bike.
questions.explanation: Road and traffic conditions change constantly. The safest lane position also changes. Choose the position that gives you the most space around your bike and lets other drivers see you best.

questions.question: You should increase your following distance if:

options.text: The pavement is dry.
The pavement is wet.
You can see through the vehicle ahead of you.
The sun is out.

questions.correctAnswerText: The pavement is wet.
questions.explanation: You need more space if your motorcycle takes longer to stop. This includes wet or slippery roads, when you cannot see through the vehicle ahead, or when traffic is heavy and another driver might cut in front of you.

questions.question: One way to tell if your rear tire has gone flat while riding is if:

options.text: There is a hissing noise coming from the rear of the bike.
The back end jerks from side to side.
You cannot accelerate.
The rear brake does not work.

questions.correctAnswerText: The back end jerks from side to side.
questions.explanation: When your rear tire fails, the back of your motorcycle will jerk side to side. Riders rarely hear a tire fail while riding.

questions.question: Usually, a good way to handle a tailgater is to:

options.text: Move onto the shoulder to get out of their way.
Speed up to put distance between you and the tailgater.
Ignore them.
Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. Change lanes safely and let them pass. Speeding up may make it more dangerous by making them follow you faster.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Is not necessary if you have a windshield.
Only protects your eyes.
Helps protect your whole face.
Does not protect your face as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps protect your whole face.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes, not your whole face. A windshield is not enough protection instead of a face shield or goggles.
